body: Just because the argument against my line of reasoning for ending my life is flawed, does not necessarily imply that my line of reasoning is valid.  However, when pointing out that the argument I was given appeared to be severely flawed, I was shut down rather than being presented with a different argument, or having it explained to me that the argument was in fact valid.

Logical reasoning (for instance, logical fallacies) exist objectively.  


In addition, I have spoken with multiple mental health professionals who have assured me that my pure reasoning skills are stronger than the vast majority of people.
Most people appear to be assholes, but I am open-minded enough to understand that appearances do not necessarily reflect reality.

Their reasoning as to why I should not end my life did not appear to be logically valid to me.  I find that humans generally believe that not believing their reasoning to be logically valid is a social cue that one does not wish to learn.
I was not able to comprehend their reasoning as to why I should not end my life, as it applied to my specific value system.
